SOURCE EXTRACT — read from cached annual reports, 2026-09-06 (p_438)
=====================================================================
YMCA OF MONTREAL, ANNUAL REPORTS FOR 1890-91, 1891-92 AND 1892-93
Already in this repo's cache. Read here for the Cushings, which no previous pass had done.

WHY: the Year Book established that a CHARLES CUSHING of Montreal held the YMCA's corresponding
membership for Quebec from 1887 to at least 1895 (f_4987), and the identification with Lemuel
Cushing Sr.'s son rested on name, city, period and calling. p_438 asked whether the association's
own records would close that, and whether any Cushing sat close enough to the 1892 Lake
Saint-Joseph trip to make it an association initiative rather than a private one.

They do, and the answer to the second question is that FOUR CUSHINGS WERE INSIDE THE ASSOCIATION
AT ONCE.


I. THE OFFICERS AND STAFF, 1892-93 — THE YEAR OF THE TRIP AND THE COMMITTEE
===========================================================================
From the report for the year ending 30 April 1893, quoted with the OCR's slips left in:

    President.                  [name lost to the scan]
    Vice-President.             WILLIAM TEES.
    Treasurer.                  WARDEN KING.
    Recording Secretary.        CHAS. CUSHING,
    Board of Directors.
      Term expires May 1st, 1894.   WARDEN KING.      R. HENRY HOLLAND.
                                    L. H. PACKARD.    SETH P. LEET.
                                    W. GODBEE BROWN.  Dr. F. W. KELLEY.
      Term expires May 1st, 1896.   CHAS. T. WILLIAMS. GEORGE LAMB.
                                    WALTER PAUL. GEORGE HAGUE. FRED. MEYERS.

    D. A. BUDGE .................... General Secretary.
    T. DUNCAN PATTON ............... Assistant Secretary.
    PERCY H. CUSHING ............... [the title is OCR'd "sp be" and CANNOT BE READ]
    W. H. BALL ..................... Physical Director.
    C. B. POWTER ................... "Asset." — i.e. Asst., following Ball

TWO CAUTIONS ON THAT LIST, because the temptation is to tidy it.
  PERCY H. CUSHING'S TITLE IS ILLEGIBLE. He is unambiguously IN THE STAFF LIST, between the
    Assistant Secretary and the Physical Director, so he is on the association's staff in 1892-93.
    What he was called is not recoverable from this scan and is NOT supplied here.
  C. B. POWTER'S TITLE IS ONE MANGLED WORD, "Asset.", immediately under Ball as Physical Director.
    "Asst." is the obvious reading and Assistant Physical Director the obvious sense — the 1896
    Year Book gives him exactly that under exactly Ball — but the label as printed here is one
    OCR'd word and is quoted rather than expanded.


II. WHAT THIS SETTLES ABOUT CHARLES CUSHING
===========================================
He is on the BOARD OF DIRECTORS of the Montreal YMCA in all three reports — 1890-91, 1891-92 and
1892-93 — listed among "ABNER KINGMAN, ROBERT HENDERSON, JOHN KENNEDY, CHARLES CUSHING, WM. TEES,
DAVID YUILE" — and by 1892-93 he is the association's RECORDING SECRETARY. He also appears in the
subscription lists ("Cushing, Chas ... 15 00").

So a Charles Cushing of Montreal sat on the association's board and served as its recording
secretary in exactly the years a Charles Cushing of Montreal was the International Committee's
corresponding member for Quebec. THAT IS THE SAME MAN BY ANY REASONABLE READING, and it removes
the last softness from f_4987's identification — though no single document still says so in one
line, and that is how it is written.

A NEAT CORROBORATION IN PASSING: WILLIAM TEES sits beside him on the same board, and is
VICE-PRESIDENT in 1892-93. Tees is the man who takes over the Quebec corresponding membership by
the 1897 Year Book. The post passed from one Montreal board member to another.


III. THE OTHER THREE CUSHINGS
=============================
PERCY H. CUSHING. On the staff in 1892-93, as above. And earlier, in the report for 1890-91, in
the Boys' Department's own account:

    "At the request of this Department, a recommendation was sent to the Provincial Committee, to
    have 'boys' work' brought prominently before the Kingston Convention. This was agreed, and a
    paper was presented by Mr. Percy H. Cushing. As a result, A NEW INTEREST WAS AWAKENED FOR WORK
    AMONG BOYS, which led to the revival of old meetings and the formation of new."

The same section opens: "We also feel the need of a Secretary who will be able to devote his whole
time to this department."

He is also "P. H. Cushing, Secretary" of a committee in the 1892-93 report, and appears in the
1891-92 committee lists. This puts him in the association's boys' work FOUR YEARS EARLIER than the
1894 Year Book, which is all this project had of him.

W. E. CUSHING. In 1890-91 he is CHAIRMAN of a committee formed to supervise work at the Methodist
Institute. He is in the committee lists of 1891-92 and 1892-93. This is the "W. E. Cushing" the
1951 camp history names on the committee appointed in the autumn of 1892 alongside J. W. Ross,
W. W. Wilson, T. Duncan Patton and W. H. Ball.

WALTER CUSHING. In the 1891-92 report, on a committee with W. Bell Dawson, W. A. Gandle, J. A.
McGregor and A. O. Dawson. Walter Edgar Cushing, Lemuel Jr.'s eldest son, was 21 that year. The
name is given as "Walter Cushing" and the identification with W. E. Cushing is NOT made here —
this project's Cushing family article already notes that Walter Edgar may have been referred to
informally by the family name, and two men or one is not settled by these lists.


IV. WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE 1892 TRIP, STATED NO FURTHER THAN IT GOES
===================================================================
p_438 asked whether the Lake Saint-Joseph trip of 1892 was an association initiative rather than a
private one the association later absorbed. These reports do not say. What they establish is the
setting:

In the year the trip happened and the founding committee was appointed, the Montreal YMCA's
recording secretary was a Cushing, a Cushing was on its staff, a Cushing chaired one of its
committees, and a fourth Cushing sat on another. Its Physical Director was W. H. Ball and its
Assistant Secretary was T. Duncan Patton — two of the five men the 1951 history names on that
committee. Percy H. Cushing had, two years earlier, been the man the department sent to argue
boys' work before a national convention, "as a result" of which "a new interest was awakened for
work among boys".

THAT IS A DENSE INSTITUTIONAL SETTING, NOT A DOCUMENT. None of these reports mentions Lake
Saint-Joseph, a camp, or a summer outing in the passages read. The trip may still have been
private. But "a private initiative the association later absorbed" now has to explain why the
family running it held the recording secretaryship, a staff post and two committee chairs at the
time — and the honest version of this project's open question is no longer "was a Cushing
involved" but "did the association minute it".

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the Boys' Department's own section in the 1892-93 and 1893-94 reports, read
in full rather than searched for a surname; and the committee minute books in the Concordia fonds.
THE REPORTS WERE SEARCHED HERE FOR CUSHING AND NOT READ THROUGH — that is the next pass, and it is
a pass over files already on disk.

QUERIES RUN: /[CG]ushing/ case-insensitive across the 1890-91, 1891-92, 1892-93, 1893-94, 1894-95
and 1895-96 reports (4, 7, 9, 14, 11 and 13 hits); the 1890-91, 1891-92 and 1892-93 hits read in
context; repo-wide greps on "Recording Secretary", "PERCY H. CUSHING", "Kingston Convention",
"William Tees" and "Wm. Tees" before anything was called new. THE 1893-94, 1894-95 AND 1895-96
REPORTS WERE COUNTED BUT THEIR HITS WERE NOT READ.
